name: Kids
description: Server side of kids mode for Jellyfin clients such as Peke for Jellyfin: kid profiles with avatars, a household parent lock, screen time shared across devices and per-kid live TV, through an API any client can use.

versions.changelog: Configure a kid from one place. The kid editor (Dashboard → Kids → a kid) now has four tabs: Kids, with the plugin's settings as before, and Profile, Access and Parental control, which repeat the parts of Jellyfin's own user pages that matter for a kid: Live TV access and downloads (and administrator, shown only so it can be turned off), which libraries the kid can see, the maximum rating, blocking unrated items and the allowed hours. Each tab saves on its own the way Jellyfin does: it reads the user again and changes only its own fields, so nothing else in the policy is lost, and a change Jellyfin refuses shows its reason in the tab. A tab with unsaved changes is marked. The Fix links of the protection check open the right tab, and each tab links to the kid in Jellyfin's Users pages. No API or database change.

The plugin's data moves to a safe place. The database (kid profiles, the parent code verifier, screen time, bonuses, channels and picks) used to live in plugins/Jellyfin.Plugin.Kids/, next to the plugin's install folder, where it looked like a stray old install. It now lives in data/kids/kids.db in Jellyfin's data folder, next to Jellyfin's own database (for example /var/lib/jellyfin/data/kids/, or /config/data/kids/ in Docker). On its first start this version moves it: it copies the database with SQLite's backup (pending write-ahead log changes included), checks the copy (integrity check, same schema version, same rows in every table), switches to it, and renames the old file kids.db.migrated-<date>, kept for one release. Every step is logged, and an interrupted move resumes at the next start. A locked or damaged old database is left untouched and nothing is created; if both folders hold a database the one written later is used and the other kept as kids.db.older-<date-time>, or the plugin refuses with an error when it cannot tell. A README.txt in the folder says what it is and not to delete it. Dashboard → Kids shows the data folder under Data (GET /Kids/Admin/Storage, administrators only). Jellyfin's own backup does not include plugin data: back up the folder (see docs/install.md, "Your data"). Downgrading to 0.0.9.0 starts with no kids unless you copy data/kids/kids.db back to plugins/Jellyfin.Plugin.Kids/ first.

Undo a bonus: POST /Kids/Users/{id}/WatchTime/Bonus now answers the new bonus's id and until when it can be undone. An administrator or a parent grant holder can undo it with DELETE /Kids/Users/{id}/WatchTime/Bonus/{bonusId} within 10 minutes on the same day, and gets the kid's new status (time's up can come back). Ids are never reused, so two TVs never undo each other's bonus. GET /Kids/Users/{id}/WatchTime/Bonus lists today's bonuses. Bonuses given with a parent grant are recorded as such. Undos are logged. End a break: POST /Kids/Users/{id}/WatchTime/Break/End lets a kid in the break after their sitting limit watch again at once, keeping today's used time and bonus; the next sitting starts from zero at the next playback. Logged. GET /Kids/Info reports API 1.2 (ApiMinorVersion 2) with the bonusUndo and breakEnd capabilities. The kid editor lists today's bonuses with Undo and shows End break during a break. The plugin database moves to schema 5.

Kids dashboard: each kid row says what still leaves the kid unprotected (an administrator account, every library, no maximum rating, unrated movies and shows, live TV access out of step with the picked channels, downloads), each with a Fix link to the right tab of Jellyfin's user editor. A banner at the top says when limits only apply in Wholphin (enforcement off, with a Turn on button) or when routes cannot be guarded, and kid rows show an "App only" pill meanwhile. The daily allowance and the sitting limit get explicit "No limit" choices, and an allowance of 0 reads "No screen time today". Rows and the editor show "Watches N of M channels" or "No live TV", the server time with its UTC offset, the household break next to the sitting limit and the kid's allowed hours. Every save confirms with a toast, and forms say when they have unsaved changes. Reset today: POST /Kids/Users/{id}/WatchTime/Reset (administrator or parent grant) sets the kid's used time and bonus for today back to 0 and lifts a stop for time or the sitting limit at once; it is logged (capability watchTimeReset). The kid editor has a Reset today button.

UPGRADE NOTE: this update cuts every kid's live TV until a parent picks their channels (Dashboard → Kids → the kid → "Live TV channels"), even with enforcement off. Live TV for kids: each kid's profile lists the live TV channels they may watch. Always on, whatever EnforcementEnabled says: on every client a kid can only play, list and see the guide of their own channels, and recordings and timers are refused. Live TV counts as screen time like any playback. Kids read their channels and guide from /Kids/Users/{id}/LiveTv/Channels and /LiveTv/Programs (capability liveTv).

Dashboard controls for enforcement: an "Enforce on every app" switch, the break between sittings (1–240 minutes) and the playback-route self-check on the Kids page; the kid editor shows the current sitting and any refusal.

Enforcement (off by default, EnforcementEnabled in the plugin configuration): the server warns, stops and refuses playback on every client when a kid's allowance, allowed hours or sitting limit runs out; Status reports the denial and the sitting, counted per kid across devices with a household break (SittingBreakMinutes, default 15).

Dashboard pages redesigned to look and behave like native Jellyfin 12.2 pages: a max-width layout, the users list first with avatars, full names, today's screen time and a visible Edit settings button, then the parent lock and screen time; the kid editor grouped into sections, with bonus minutes moved into it.
Session limit: an optional per-kid sitting limit (5–120 minutes) in the kid profile and the dashboard editor, stored by the server and counted by each TV.
